title: Chain-of-Thought Is Not Explainability
abstract: arXiv:2611.31271v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) allows language models to verbalise multi-step rationales before producing their final answer. While this technique often boosts task performance and offers an impression of transparency into the model's reasoning, this position paper argues that rationales generated by current CoT techniques can be misleading and are neither necessary nor sufficient for trustworthy interpretability. We analyse faithfulness as whether CoTs are not only human-interpretable but also reflect the model's underlying reasoning well enough to support responsible use. By synthesising evidence from prior work, we systematically show that verbalised chains are frequently unfaithful, diverging from the critical hidden computations that drive a model's predictions. translated_abstract: 思维链（CoT）允许语言模型在给出最终答案之前，以语言形式表达多步推理过程。虽然这一技术通常能提升任务表现，并给人一种洞察模型推理过程的透明感，但本立场论文认为，当前CoT技术生成的推理说明可能具有误导性，对于可信的可解释性而言既非必要也非充分条件。我们将忠实性界定为：CoT不仅应当对人类可理解，还应当足够好地反映模型的底层推理过程，以支持负责任的使用。通过综合先前工作的证据，我们系统地表明，语言化的推理链经常是不忠实的，与驱动模型预测的关键隐藏计算相背离。随着CoT在各类应用领域（包括医疗、法律和自主系统等高风险领域）中被日益依赖，我们进一步认为，这种不忠实性并非……（摘要截断）
tldr: 本立场论文指出，思维链生成的推理说明经常不忠实于模型真实的内部隐藏计算，因而不能作为可信的可解释性依据，既非必要也非充分。
en_tdlr: This position paper argues that chain-of-thought rationales are frequently unfaithful to the model's underlying hidden computations, and are therefore neither necessary nor sufficient for trustworthy explainability.
